summary: EarthPulse is a web app that turns NASA Earth observation data into plain-language, location-specific status for wildfire, flood risk, soil moisture and air quality. details:
EarthPulse is a web app that turns NASA Earth observation data into plain-language, location-specific status for four hazards: wildfire, flood risk, soil moisture and air quality. A user searches for a place and sees a Nominal, Watch, Warning or Critical status for each hazard, a short explanation, a 7-day trend, and a satellite map with fire and flood markers [and a date scrubber].

The app uses NASA FIRMS fire detections, NASA EONET natural events, NASA GIBS satellite imagery, and NASA POWER rainfall and soil moisture data. It also uses Open-Meteo for air quality and river-flow forecasts. Open-Meteo is not NASA data, and the app labels it as partner data. A rule-based risk engine with published thresholds turns the numbers into statuses. The Gemini API then writes a short plain-language brief using only the data the app fetched. [Users can choose a role (farmer, hiker, responder or planner) and get actions tailored to it, in English and Urdu.]

Benefits
Users don’t need any remote-sensing expertise. They get one screen for their exact place, a clear status and concrete actions. Every number shows its source and update time, and a “Why this status” section explains the rule behind it. The app is free to run because it uses open data and needs no account.

Intended impact
We want to close the gap between satellite data and everyday decisions for people in flood- and fire-prone regions such as Pakistan. The next steps are SMS and WhatsApp alerts, offline mode, voice in local languages, and testing with farmers and rescue teams.

Tools and technology
We built the app in Google AI Studio with Gemini and deployed it on Vercel. [It uses React, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS and Leaflet for the map.] It calls the NASA and Open-Meteo APIs listed above. It needs no special hardware.

What is creative about it
Most Earth-data tools are portals built for experts. EarthPulse acts as a translation layer: one status per hazard, plus actions for each role. Its status language is inspired by mission control. It is transparent about which data comes from NASA and which doesn’t. It is bilingual from the start.
dataRefs: NASA FIRMS (Fire Information for Resource Management System)
NASA EONET (Earth Observatory Natural Event Tracker)
